title: HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF FISHERIES
body_text:
The fisheries sector is one of the fastest-growing agri-allied sectors in the country and plays a significant role in economic growth, food and nutritional securities, employment generation, livelihood support and export earnings. Under entry 21 of List-II of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India – “ Fisheries ” is within the purview of the State Governments. Whereas under entry 57 of List-I of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India – “ Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters ” is within the mandate of the Union of India. The fisheries sector, during 2023-24 has contributed about 7.43% to the Agricultural Gross Value Added (GVA) and about 1.09% to the country's total GVA.
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has taken up several steps for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector including welfare of fishers and fish farmers in the country. The steps taken up include implementation of fisheries and aquaculture development schemes such as (i) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), (ii) Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), (iii) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY). In addition, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018-19 has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirements.
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) implemented by the DoF, GoI inter-alia provides for one-time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by farmers. The one-time incentive for aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares Water Spread Area (WSA). For the aquaculture system including intensive systems like farms, cage culture, Recirculatory Aquaculture System (RAS), bio-floc and raceways, aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹1 lakh per farmer for 1800 m3 intensive aquaculture systems. Further, the SC/ST and women beneficiaries get an additional 10% of the incentive given to the General Category Farmers.
This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying informed the Rajya Sabha about steps taken for holistic development of India's fisheries sector, which contributed about 7.43% to Agricultural GVA and 1.09% to total GVA in 2023-24. Key initiatives include PMMSY, FIDF, PM-MKSSY, and Kisan Credit Card facility extended to fishers since 2018-19. PM-MKSSY notably offers a one-time incentive of 40% of aquaculture insurance premium (with caps of ₹25,000/hectare or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares WSA, and similar caps for intensive systems), with an additional 10% incentive for SC/ST and women beneficiaries.
enrichment.context:
Fisheries is a state subject under Entry 21 of List-II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule, while fishing beyond territorial waters falls under Union jurisdiction (Entry 57, List-I). This constitutional division shapes how the Centre supports the sector primarily through centrally sponsored schemes rather than direct implementation. The sector has been highlighted as part of the 'Blue Revolution' and is central to India's push for doubling farmers' income, food security, and export earnings (India is among the top fish and shrimp exporters globally).

PMMSY (launched 2020) is the umbrella scheme for fisheries development with an outlay of about ₹20,050 crore, aiming to enhance fish production, productivity, and infrastructure. FIDF supports infrastructure financing for fishing harbours, cold chains, and processing units. PM-MKSSY, a newer sub-scheme, focuses on formalization of the sector via registration, working capital access, and insurance incentivization to reduce risk in aquaculture, which is vulnerable to disease outbreaks and climate-related losses. Extension of KCC to fishers (since 2018-19) mirrors the agricultural credit support system, recognizing fisheries as an agri-allied activity requiring similar financial inclusion measures.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, 'Fisheries' as a general subject falls under which of the following?
options: Both Union List and State List, depending on territorial waters
prelims_questions.explanation: Entry 21 of List-II (State List) covers 'Fisheries' generally, while Entry 57 of List-I (Union List) covers 'Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters', making it a subject split between both lists based on jurisdictional territory.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following schemes provides a one-time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by fish farmers in India?
options: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PM-MKSSY provides a one-time incentive of 40% of the aquaculture insurance premium paid, subject to specified ceilings, with additional benefits for SC/ST and women beneficiaries.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the fisheries sector in India's agricultural economy. Examine the constitutional division of responsibilities between the Union and States in this sector and its implications for policy coordination.
Critically evaluate the role of centrally sponsored schemes like PM-MKSSY and PMMSY in promoting risk mitigation and financial inclusion among fish farmers in India.
